title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
About Maplestack
Maplestack builds inventory and order-management software used by more than 900 mid-market retailers across North America. Our backend platform processes several million order events a day, and we are hiring a Senior Backend Engineer to help us scale it.

What you'll do
- Design and ship Node.js services behind our public and partner APIs
- Own PostgreSQL schema design, query performance, and migration safety for high-volume tables
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor two intermediate engineers
- Improve observability (tracing, structured logs, alerting) across the order pipeline
- Participate in a humane on-call rotation (roughly one week in eight)

What we're looking for
- 5+ years building production backend systems, ideally in TypeScript or Node.js
- Deep working knowledge of PostgreSQL: indexing strategy, locking behaviour, EXPLAIN
- Experience designing versioned REST APIs consumed by external developers
- Clear written communication — most design work happens in RFC documents

Compensation & perks
$140,000–$170,000 base depending on experience, plus meaningful equity, four weeks vacation, a $1,500 learning budget, and comprehensive health/dental from day one. Hybrid: Tuesdays and Thursdays in our King West office.

Maplestack is an equal-opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates.

title: Frontend Developer (React)
description:
Cedarbyte Systems builds scheduling and dispatch software for field-service companies — plumbers, electricians, HVAC crews — across Canada and the US. Our customers live in our product all day, so the quality of the interface is the product.

The role
You'll join a six-person product engineering team and own significant pieces of our React application: the dispatch board, the technician mobile web view, and our growing internal design system.

Day to day you will
- Build accessible, performant UI in React and TypeScript
- Extend our component library and push back on inconsistent design
- Work directly with customers during beta rollouts of new workflows
- Profile and fix rendering performance issues in data-heavy views
- Write meaningful tests where they pay for themselves

You should have
- 3+ years shipping production React applications
- Strong TypeScript and a good eye for component API design
- Experience with state management beyond useState (we use a mix of server cache and local stores)
- Empathy for non-technical users under time pressure

What we offer
$95,000–$120,000 (as required by BC's Pay Transparency Act), extended health benefits, an annual profit-share, and a bright office in Gastown with bike storage. This is an in-office role with flexible hours.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Fjordline Analytics helps energy and utilities companies make sense of sensor and market data. We're a 40-person consultancy-turned-product-company headquartered in downtown Calgary, and we're hiring a Data Engineer for our platform team.

What you'll work on
- Building and maintaining ELT pipelines in Python against our cloud data warehouse
- Modelling curated datasets with dbt, including tests and documentation
- Hardening ingestion from client systems: SCADA historians, market feeds, flat-file drops
- Improving pipeline observability so failures are caught before clients notice
- Pairing with analysts to turn one-off notebooks into maintained data products

Requirements
- 3+ years in data engineering or backend engineering with heavy data exposure
- Strong SQL — window functions, incremental models, query plans
- Production Python: typing, packaging, testing
- Experience with orchestration tools (we run a managed scheduler; naming it in your cover letter is not required)
- Bonus: exposure to time-series data or the energy sector

Compensation
$110,000–$135,000, annual bonus tied to company performance, RRSP matching to 4%, and three weeks vacation to start. Relocation support available for candidates moving to Calgary.

title: Product Designer
description:
Lakefold Studios is the design-led software company behind two B2B products used by architecture and engineering firms to manage drawings, revisions, and approvals. Design isn't a service function here — half our leadership team started as designers.

What you'll do
- Own end-to-end design for one of our two products: research, flows, high-fidelity UI, and follow-through with engineering
- Run lightweight discovery calls with practising architects and project managers
- Contribute components and patterns to our shared Figma design system
- Prototype interactions that involve dense, technical data without drowning users in it
- Present work in weekly critique and give sharp, generous feedback on others' work

What we're looking for
- 3–6 years of product design experience, ideally on complex B2B tools
- A portfolio showing real shipped work and the reasoning behind it
- Fluency in Figma, including variables and component architecture
- Enough comfort with technical constraints to negotiate with engineers credibly

Details
$90,000–$115,000 depending on experience, health and dental, a four-day summer-hours pilot, and a studio in the Junction Triangle with actual natural light. Hybrid, three days a week in studio.

title: Security Analyst (SOC, Tier 2)
description:
Nightjar Security operates a 24/7 managed detection and response service for Canadian public-sector and financial clients from our Ottawa security operations centre. We're adding a Tier 2 Analyst to the day rotation.

Responsibilities
- Triage and investigate escalations from Tier 1: endpoint detections, suspicious authentication patterns, phishing reports
- Perform deeper analysis in our SIEM and EDR consoles; document findings in clear, client-readable incident notes
- Tune detection rules to cut false positives without widening blind spots
- Contribute to playbooks and mentor Tier 1 analysts on investigation technique
- Join scheduled purple-team exercises with our offensive practice

Requirements
- 2–4 years in a SOC, incident response, or security engineering role
- Comfort reading Windows and Linux logs without a dashboard holding your hand
- Working knowledge of common attacker tradecraft and the frameworks that catalogue it
- Eligibility for federal Reliability Status screening (we'll sponsor the process)

Compensation and shift details
$85,000–$105,000 plus a shift premium for weekend coverage weeks, full benefits, and a certification budget that actually gets approved. This role is on-site at our Kanata SOC.

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
Saltbox Commerce makes wholesale ordering software for food and beverage distributors. Our customers are busy operators, not software people — which is exactly why customer success is the heart of this company.

About the role
You'll own a book of roughly 60 mid-market accounts through onboarding, adoption, renewal, and expansion. This is a remote-first role; we ask for one week per quarter at our Calgary office for planning, and occasional customer site visits.

What you'll do
- Run structured onboarding that gets a distributor live in under 30 days
- Build renewal and expansion plans grounded in usage data, not vibes
- Translate recurring customer pain into crisp product feedback
- Host quarterly business reviews with owner-operators and ops managers
- Keep our CRM honest

What we're looking for
- 2+ years in customer success, account management, or implementation for a B2B software product
- Comfort discussing margins, fill rates, and other operational metrics with non-technical buyers
- Excellent writing — much of your relationship happens over email
- Bonus: food-service, distribution, or logistics industry exposure

Compensation
$75,000–$95,000 base plus a retention-linked bonus, health benefits, home-office stipend, and four weeks vacation.

title: Financial Analyst, FP&A
description:
Timberline Financial provides equipment leasing to forestry, construction, and transportation businesses across Canada. We manage a growing portfolio from our Toronto head office and are adding a Financial Analyst to the FP&A team.

The work
- Own the monthly reporting package: variance analysis, portfolio KPIs, and commentary the executive team actually reads
- Maintain and improve the rolling 18-month forecast model
- Partner with credit and operations teams to cost new initiatives and price programs
- Automate recurring reporting — we are actively moving from spreadsheet-only workflows to a warehouse-backed model, and analysts who can write SQL move faster here
- Support the annual budget cycle end to end

Your background
- 2–4 years in FP&A, corporate finance, or a Big Four/mid-tier firm looking to move into industry
- Advanced spreadsheet modelling; working SQL is a strong asset
- CPA or CFA progress is valued but not required
- You communicate numbers in plain language and flag risks early

Offer
$80,000–$95,000 plus a target bonus of 10%, RRSP matching, hybrid schedule (three days downtown), and a genuine promotion path — the last two senior analysts were promoted internally.

title: Staff Accountant
description:
Aurora Ledger is a Halifax accounting and advisory firm serving owner-managed businesses across the Maritimes — restaurants, marine services, construction, and a fast-growing roster of tech startups. We're hiring a Staff Accountant to join our core client-services team.

What you'll do
- Full-cycle bookkeeping and month-end close for a portfolio of 15–20 clients
- Prepare working papers, HST returns, and year-end files for review
- Assist with compilation engagements and T2 preparation during busy season
- Help clients modernize their record-keeping on cloud accounting platforms
- Field client questions with patience and plain language

What we're looking for
- A completed accounting degree or diploma; enrolment in the CPA program is fully supported (we pay module fees and give paid study days)
- 1–3 years of public-practice or industry accounting experience
- Tidy, well-documented working habits — your files should be reviewable without a decoder ring
- Genuine interest in small-business clients and their messy, real-world books

Why Aurora Ledger
Competitive salary commensurate with experience, paid overtime or time-in-lieu during busy season (we mean it), full benefits, and a firm culture that treats CPA students as future partners rather than throughput. Office is on Barrington Street, steps from the ferry terminal.

title: Embedded Systems Engineer
description:
Kestrel Robotics builds autonomous inspection robots for warehouses and cold-storage facilities. Our robots run 20-hour shifts in -25°C freezers, which means our firmware has to be boringly reliable in decidedly non-boring conditions.

What you'll own
- Firmware for sensor and motor-control subsystems on our embedded Linux and RTOS targets
- Drivers and communication layers (CAN, SPI, I2C) between compute modules
- Power-management logic that squeezes real mission time out of cold-soaked batteries
- Hardware bring-up for new board revisions alongside our EE team
- Field-debugging tools that let support diagnose robots without shipping them back

Must-haves
- 3+ years of embedded C/C++ in production devices
- Real-time fundamentals: interrupts, DMA, scheduling, watchdogs
- Comfort with lab equipment — scopes, logic analyzers — and reading schematics
- The judgment to know when 'works on my bench' isn't 'works in a freezer'

Nice-to-haves
- Rust curiosity, functional-safety exposure, or robotics/motion-control background

Package
$105,000–$130,000, employee stock options, comprehensive benefits, and an on-site lab in the David Johnston Research + Technology Park. Relocation assistance for candidates moving to Waterloo Region.

title: Digital Marketing Specialist
description:
Wintergreen Media is a 25-person digital agency working with consumer brands in home goods, wellness, and specialty food. We plan, launch, and optimize campaigns end to end — and we're adding a Digital Marketing Specialist to our performance team.

What the job looks like
- Build and manage paid search and paid social campaigns for 4–6 client accounts
- Own weekly optimization: budgets, bids, negative keywords, creative rotation
- Run on-page SEO audits and coordinate fixes with our content and dev partners
- Assemble clear monthly reports that connect spend to outcomes clients care about
- Test landing-page variants and document what actually moved the numbers

Who does well here
- 1–3 years of hands-on campaign management, agency or in-house
- Fluency with ad platforms and web analytics; certification is nice, judgment is nicer
- Enough spreadsheet skill to build a pivot table without googling it twice
- Curiosity about why a campaign worked, not just whether it did

Compensation and benefits
$55,000–$70,000 depending on experience, health benefits after three months, a transit-friendly office near Queen and Spadina with a hybrid schedule (two office days), and Friday afternoons off in July and August.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
Stonebridge Payments processes card-present transactions for independent grocers and pharmacies across Canada. Reliability is our entire brand: when our platform blips, someone's checkout line stops moving.

The role
We're hiring a DevOps Engineer to join the four-person platform team that owns our cloud infrastructure, deployment tooling, and observability stack.

You will
- Manage our Kubernetes clusters and the Terraform that provisions everything around them
- Improve CI/CD pipelines so product teams ship small changes safely and often
- Build and tune alerting that pages on symptoms, not noise
- Lead blameless post-incident reviews and drive the follow-ups to completion
- Help us satisfy PCI DSS obligations without smothering developer velocity

You bring
- 4+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering roles
- Production Kubernetes experience — upgrades, resource tuning, debugging weird pod states
- Infrastructure-as-code discipline and strong scripting (Bash/Python)
- Experience operating regulated or high-availability systems is a strong asset

What we offer
$115,000–$140,000, on-call premium, RRSP matching, comprehensive benefits, and a hybrid arrangement anchored to our Ottawa office (two days weekly). Security screening is required given the payments environment.

title: Content Marketing Manager
description:
Muskoka Digital builds marketing sites and content programs for professional-services firms — law, accounting, engineering — that need to sound credible without sounding embalmed. We're hiring a Content Marketing Manager to lead client content programs.

This role is remote within Canada; our editorial team is anchored in Montréal and gathers there twice a year.

What you'll do
- Own content strategy for 5–7 client accounts: positioning, editorial calendars, and measurement
- Write and edit cornerstone pieces yourself — this is a player-coach role
- Manage a bench of freelance writers, briefing them well enough that drafts arrive usable
- Work with our SEO lead to target topics that earn qualified traffic, not vanity impressions
- Report results to clients in language their managing partners respect

You're a fit if you have
- 4+ years in content marketing, journalism, or communications, some of it managing other writers
- A portfolio of published B2B writing you're proud of
- Working SEO literacy: search intent, on-page fundamentals, internal linking
- Bilingual English/French is a meaningful asset for two of our accounts

Compensation
$70,000–$90,000, four weeks vacation, health benefits, home-office budget, and a profession-development allowance.

title: Site Reliability Engineer
description:
Cordillera Cloud runs managed data infrastructure for media and gaming companies with spiky, unforgiving traffic patterns. Our SRE team keeps hundreds of clusters healthy across three cloud regions.

About the role
This is a remote-first position for candidates based in Canada (Pacific or Mountain time preferred for on-call overlap). The team meets quarterly in Vancouver.

What you'll do
- Define and defend SLOs for our managed platform; make error budgets mean something
- Build automation that eliminates entire categories of toil — runbooks are a bug report
- Deepen our observability stack: metrics, traces, and logs that answer questions fast
- Lead capacity planning ahead of client launch events and seasonal peaks
- Take part in a compensated on-call rotation with real handoffs and real quiet weeks

What we're looking for
- 4+ years in SRE, platform, or infrastructure roles operating systems at scale
- Strong Linux internals and network debugging instincts
- Production experience on at least one major cloud provider
- Code fluency in Go or Python beyond scripting
- Calm, structured incident leadership

Compensation
$130,000–$160,000 (BC Pay Transparency Act range), on-call compensation on top, extended benefits, RRSP matching, and a hardware budget refreshed every three years.

title: Medical Office Administrator
description:
Redcap Health operates three multidisciplinary clinics on Prince Edward Island offering family medicine, physiotherapy, and mental-health services. Our Charlottetown clinic is hiring a full-time Medical Office Administrator.

What you'll do
- Manage the front desk: greet patients, verify health cards, and keep the waiting room running on time
- Book and confirm appointments across five practitioners' schedules in our electronic medical record system
- Process referrals, requisitions, and incoming records with strict attention to privacy
- Handle billing submissions and reconcile rejected claims
- Order clinic supplies and coordinate with our other two locations

What we're looking for
- Medical office administration diploma, or equivalent front-desk experience in a healthcare setting
- Comfort learning clinical software quickly; prior EMR experience is a strong asset
- A calm, warm manner with patients who may be anxious, unwell, or frustrated
- Discretion — you will handle sensitive personal health information daily and are expected to treat it accordingly

Details
This is a permanent, full-time position (Monday–Friday, occasional Saturday rotation). Compensation is competitive for the Island market with health benefits, paid sick days, and free parking. Please include a short note about your experience handling confidential information.

title: QA Analyst
description:
Prairie Circuit develops point-of-sale and back-office software for agricultural retailers — the co-ops and input suppliers that keep Prairie farms running. Twelve hundred locations depend on our releases being right the first time.

The role
We're hiring a QA Analyst to join our Winnipeg product team. You'll be the quality conscience for two delivery squads.

Responsibilities
- Design test plans for new features, from happy path to the weird edge cases retail throws at software
- Extend our automated regression suite (browser-based, with a modern test runner) and keep it fast and trustworthy
- Reproduce field-reported defects, narrow them to root cause, and write reports developers thank you for
- Own release sign-off checklists for our quarterly on-premise releases
- Advocate for testability during design discussions, not after

Qualifications
- 2+ years in software QA, with at least some hands-on test automation
- Enough SQL to verify data outcomes directly
- Methodical documentation habits and a sceptical mind
- Retail, POS, or agriculture domain exposure is an asset, not a requirement

What we offer
Competitive salary based on experience, full benefits including a health spending account, an on-site gym, profit sharing, and a stable, profitable company that has never had a layoff in 19 years.

title: Operations Coordinator
description:
Fleuve Logistics coordinates less-than-truckload freight between Québec and the U.S. Northeast from our Longueuil terminal. We're a family-owned carrier with 85 trucks, a modern fleet, and a dispatch office that runs on coffee and precision.

Le poste / The role
We're hiring an Operations Coordinator to support our dispatch and customer-service functions. Working language is French; functional English is required for U.S. partner carriers and customers.

What you'll do
- Build and adjust daily load plans with dispatchers as pickups shift
- Enter orders, confirm appointments, and keep our ERP records clean
- Track shipments and proactively call customers before they call us
- Prepare customs paperwork packages and chase missing documents
- Compile weekly on-time and claims metrics for the operations manager

Profile
- 1–3 years in logistics, transport, or a fast-paced coordination role
- Bilingual French/English (spoken and written)
- Composure when three phones ring at once and a border crossing just backed up
- Comfort with ERP or TMS systems, and spreadsheets that don't scare you

Conditions
$60,000–$75,000 depending on experience, group insurance, RRSP with employer contribution, on-site parking, and a real path into dispatch or customer-experience management.

title: Curriculum Developer (EdTech)
description:
Birchside Learning builds workplace-safety and compliance training used by more than 400 Canadian employers in construction, manufacturing, and utilities. Our courses are the opposite of the click-next-to-continue slog you're imagining — and we intend to keep it that way.

About the role
This is a remote role within Canada (our studio is in Toronto, and you're welcome at the desk anytime). You'll join a team of four curriculum developers working alongside media producers and subject-matter experts.

What you'll do
- Turn dense regulatory material into scenario-based learning that tradespeople respect
- Write scripts, storyboards, knowledge checks, and assessments
- Build and publish courses in our LMS authoring pipeline, including accessibility passes (WCAG AA)
- Interview safety officers, operators, and trainers to ground courses in reality
- Analyze completion and assessment data to find and fix weak modules

What we're looking for
- 3+ years in instructional design or curriculum development, ideally for adult learners
- Exceptionally clear writing — send samples; they matter more than the resume
- Familiarity with SCORM/xAPI publishing workflows
- Bonus: trades, OHS, or industrial training background

Compensation
$78,000–$96,000 (Ontario pay-transparency range), four weeks vacation, benefits from day one, and an annual conference-or-course allowance.

title: Industrial Millwright
description:
Copperline Manufacturing produces steel wire and cable products at our Sydney, Nova Scotia plant, supplying utilities and marine customers across Atlantic Canada. We are hiring a certified Industrial Millwright for our maintenance team.

The work
- Preventive and corrective maintenance on drawing machines, stranders, extruders, and plant utilities
- Troubleshoot mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems under production pressure
- Precision alignment, bearing replacement, gearbox rebuilds, and conveyor work
- Fabrication and welding as required (an asset, not a daily expectation)
- Document work orders in our CMMS and contribute to reliability improvements

Requirements
- Red Seal Industrial Mechanic (Millwright) certification, or provincial equivalent with eligibility
- 3+ years of industrial plant maintenance experience
- Ability to read hydraulic schematics and mechanical drawings
- Comfortable with a rotating 12-hour shift pattern (days/nights, averaging 42 hrs/week)

What we offer
Competitive hourly wage per our collective agreement with substantial shift and overtime premiums, defined-benefit pension, full family benefits, tool allowance, and paid training. Relocation support available — Cape Breton offers a cost of living your mainland friends will envy.

title: Mobile Developer (iOS)
description:
Yellowbird Payments builds a mobile-first expense and corporate-card product for Canadian small businesses. Our iOS app is the primary surface for 60,000 monthly users, and its App Store rating is a company-level KPI.

What you'll do
- Ship features across the card-management, receipts, and approvals experiences in Swift and SwiftUI
- Push our modularization effort forward so build times stay sane as the app grows
- Sweat the details: haptics, animation timing, offline behaviour, accessibility
- Work tightly with design and backend engineers in a squad that owns outcomes, not tickets
- Harden security-sensitive flows (biometrics, secure storage, certificate pinning) with our security team

What we're looking for
- 3+ years of professional iOS development with shipped apps you can point to
- Strong Swift, solid grasp of concurrency, and real SwiftUI production experience
- Care for testing where it counts: snapshot tests for UI, unit tests for money math
- Fintech, banking, or payments experience is an asset; curiosity about it is mandatory

Package
$110,000–$135,000 plus equity, comprehensive benefits, a hybrid schedule (two days in our downtown Toronto office), and a device lab that includes the weird old iPhones your edge cases live on.

title: Motion Designer
description:
Longhouse Interactive is a Victoria-based creative studio producing brand films, product launch videos, and interactive installations for clients in tourism, tech, and public institutions. We're hiring a Motion Designer to join our post-production team.

What you'll do
- Design and animate 2D motion graphics for brand and product work — type, logo systems, data visualization, character-adjacent illustration
- Build animation toolkits and templates that keep multi-deliverable campaigns consistent
- Collaborate with editors and sound designers to hit emotional beats, not just deadlines
- Prepare deliverables across broadcast, social, and installation formats
- Pitch in on storyboards and style frames during concept development

What we're looking for
- 2–5 years of professional motion design work with a reel that shows range and restraint
- Expert After Effects; comfort in the broader Adobe suite
- Typography fundamentals strong enough to survive our creative director's review
- Experience with 3D tools or shader-based workflows is a bonus, not a requirement
- Ability to take feedback in stride and iterate quickly

Details
$65,000–$85,000 (BC pay-transparency range), extended health, flexible hours around render queues, and a harbour-view studio in Victoria's Chinatown. Hybrid possible after probation; core collaboration days are Tuesday–Thursday.

title: Supply Chain Analyst
description:
Tundra North Logistics manages inbound freight, warehousing, and distribution for retailers and industrial customers across Newfoundland and Labrador. From our Corner Brook operations centre we keep shelves stocked in communities where a missed sailing means empty aisles.

The role
We're hiring a Supply Chain Analyst to strengthen demand planning and inventory decisions across our network.

Responsibilities
- Build demand forecasts that respect island realities: ferry schedules, weather windows, seasonal swings
- Analyze inventory positions across three warehouses and recommend rebalancing before stockouts happen
- Track carrier performance and cost per lane; prepare quarterly reviews with our partners
- Write and maintain the SQL queries and reports our operations managers rely on daily
- Support the annual network review with scenario modelling

What you bring
- Degree or diploma in supply chain, business, economics, or a related field
- 1–3 years in supply chain, logistics, or analytical operations roles
- Practical SQL and strong spreadsheet modelling
- Clear communication with warehouse leads, carriers, and executives alike

What we offer
Competitive salary based on experience, health and dental benefits, RRSP matching, relocation assistance, and the kind of real-world logistics problems that make textbook cases look quaint.

title: Heavy-Duty Equipment Mechanic
description:
Quartzline Mining Tech services and rebuilds heavy equipment for placer and hard-rock operations across the Yukon. Our Whitehorse shop and field trucks keep loaders, excavators, and haul trucks running through seasons that don't forgive sloppy work.

The job
- Diagnose and repair diesel engines, hydraulics, powertrains, and electrical systems on major-brand heavy equipment
- Split time between our heated Whitehorse shop and field calls to sites within day-trip range (occasional fly-in work, always voluntary, always premium-paid)
- Perform component rebuilds and seasonal refits during the winter shop season
- Complete inspection reports and parts orders in our service software
- Mentor apprentices — we run two through their hours at any given time

Requirements
- Red Seal Heavy Duty Equipment Technician (or provincial/territorial certification with interprovincial eligibility)
- 4+ years post-ticket experience, mining or forestry equipment preferred
- Valid Class 5 licence; Class 3 with air an asset for our service trucks
- Self-sufficiency and judgment — in the field, you are the second opinion

Compensation
$95,000–$115,000 depending on experience and ticket stack, field premiums, tool allowance, full benefits, three weeks vacation to start, and a northern living allowance.

title: Brand Manager
description:
Silvermaple Foods makes maple-forward snacks and pantry staples sold in 4,000 grocery stores across Canada and a growing U.S. natural-foods channel. From our Montréal head office, we're hiring a Brand Manager to own our flagship snack line.

What you'll do
- Own the P&L, positioning, and annual brand plan for a $12M product line
- Lead pack refreshes and new-flavour launches from concept through shelf
- Partner with sales on retailer presentations, promotions, and trade-spend decisions
- Brief and manage agency partners on campaigns across retail media and social
- Mine consumption and panel data for the insight everyone else missed
- Work hand-in-hand with operations on forecasts so marketing promises match plant capacity

Profile
- 4–6 years in CPG brand management or associate brand roles
- Fluently bilingual (French/English) — you'll present in both, sometimes in the same meeting
- Strong analytical chops with syndicated retail data
- A portfolio of shipped launches with honest post-mortems

What we offer
Competitive salary with target bonus, full benefits, a hybrid schedule (three days at our Mile-End office), a snack cupboard that needs no elaboration, and a brand you can taste.

title: Warehouse Team Lead (Afternoons)
description:
Harbourline Distribution runs a 220,000 sq ft distribution centre in Winnipeg serving retail and food-service customers across Western Canada. We're hiring a Team Lead for our afternoon shift (2:00 PM – 10:30 PM, Monday–Friday).

What you'll do
- Lead a crew of 12–15 warehouse associates through picking, replenishment, and outbound loading
- Run shift start-up huddles, assign work in the WMS, and rebalance as priorities shift
- Coach new hires on safe, accurate technique; hold the line on safety standards without theatrics
- Investigate discrepancies and close out shift paperwork accurately
- Operate reach truck and counterbalance forklift as needed (certification maintained on our dime)

What we're looking for
- 2+ years of warehouse experience with at least 1 year in a lead-hand or supervisory capacity
- Working knowledge of WMS-directed workflows and RF scanning
- Valid forklift certification (or eligibility to recertify immediately)
- A calm, direct leadership style — the shift takes its temperature from you

Why Harbourline
Competitive hourly wage plus afternoon-shift premium, overtime after 8 hours, full benefits after 90 days, boot allowance, RRSP matching, and genuine advancement — both of our current supervisors started on the floor.

title: Account Executive, Mid-Market
description:
Velocity North sells compliance-automation software to Canadian financial-services firms — the unglamorous, absolutely mandatory work our buyers are thrilled to stop doing by hand. We're adding a Mid-Market Account Executive to our Toronto sales team.

The role
- Run a full-cycle sales process on inbound-qualified and self-sourced pipeline: discovery, demo, business case, procurement, close
- Sell into compliance and operations leaders at firms of 100–1,000 employees
- Keep an honest, current pipeline in the CRM — forecasting is a craft here, not a guess
- Partner with customer success on clean handoffs that set accounts up to renew
- Feed real objections back to product and marketing so the whole machine improves

What we're looking for
- 2–4 years of closing experience in B2B software, or an exceptional SDR record ready for the step up
- Discipline in qualification — we would rather you disqualify early than haunt a dead deal
- Curiosity about regulated industries; you'll need to speak our buyers' language within a quarter
- Grit without cynicism

Compensation
$75,000–$90,000 base (Ontario posting range) with uncapped variable; on-target earnings roughly double base. Benefits from day one, hybrid downtown office, presidents-club trip that people actually want to win.

title: Full-Stack Developer
description:
Wolfe Sound Software builds licensing and royalty-management tools for independent music labels and publishers. Our platform tracks rights and payments for two million recordings, and our customers finally get paid what they're owed.

About the role
We're hiring a Full-Stack Developer for our Montréal team (hybrid, two days weekly at our Plateau office; English-first engineering culture, French welcome partout).

What you'll build
- Features across our React front end and Node.js API — royalty statements, catalogue management, payout flows
- PostgreSQL schemas and queries where correctness is measured in someone's rent money
- Integrations with streaming-platform reporting feeds, in formats of, let's say, varying dignity
- Internal tools that let our support team resolve label questions without engineering help

What we're looking for
- 3+ years of full-stack development in production
- Solid TypeScript on both ends of the wire
- SQL confidence — joins and window functions shouldn't scare you, money math definitely shouldn't
- An ear for detail; our domain rewards people who read the spec twice

What we offer
$95,000–$125,000 depending on experience, four weeks vacation, full group insurance, transit pass reimbursement, and concert tickets on the company more often than is fiscally prudent.

title: Clinical Research Coordinator
description:
Tidewater BioSciences runs early- and mid-phase clinical trials in respiratory and metabolic disease at our Hamilton research clinic, in partnership with academic investigators and sponsor companies. We're hiring a Clinical Research Coordinator.

Responsibilities
- Coordinate day-to-day conduct of 3–4 concurrent studies: screening, enrolment visits, follow-ups, and close-out
- Ensure protocol adherence and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance in everything from consent to sample handling
- Maintain source documents, case report forms, and regulatory binders audit-ready at all times
- Schedule participants and act as their consistent, humane point of contact through the study
- Liaise with sponsors, monitors, and our research ethics board; prepare for and support monitoring visits
- Manage investigational product accountability with the study pharmacist

Qualifications
- Degree in health sciences, nursing, or a related field
- 1–3 years of clinical research experience; current GCP certification (or willingness to complete ours in week one)
- Meticulous documentation habits — in this job, if it isn't written down, it didn't happen
- Warm professionalism with participants, including anxious first-timers

Offer
$62,000–$78,000 depending on experience, health benefits, paid conference attendance, and a team that celebrates database lock like a playoff win.

title: SEO Specialist
description:
Urban Antler Marketing is a Kelowna agency serving home-services, tourism, and healthcare clients across the B.C. Interior. Search is our biggest channel and our best-kept promise: we rank clients for terms that actually ring their phones.

What you'll do
- Own SEO strategy and execution for a portfolio of 8–10 local and regional clients
- Run technical audits (crawlability, indexation, page experience) and shepherd fixes through client webmasters or our dev team
- Build keyword strategies rooted in search intent and local geography
- Brief content writers and edit drafts so they earn links and answer real questions
- Manage local presence: business profiles, citations, review strategy
- Report monthly in terms of leads and revenue, not just positions

What we're looking for
- 2+ years of hands-on SEO work with results you can walk us through in detail
- Fluency with crawling tools, search analytics platforms, and spreadsheet analysis
- Enough HTML and site-architecture literacy to write dev tickets that get implemented correctly
- Local SEO experience is a genuine advantage in our client mix

Details
$60,000–$75,000 (BC pay-transparency range), extended health, hybrid schedule after onboarding, half-day Fridays year-round, and an office ten minutes from the lake.

title: E-commerce Manager
description:
Glacier Peak Outfitters designs and sells technical outdoor apparel from our Vancouver headquarters, with a flagship store on West 4th and a direct-to-consumer channel that now drives most of our growth. We're hiring an E-commerce Manager to own the online business end to end.

What you'll own
- The e-commerce P&L: traffic, conversion, average order value, and returns
- Site merchandising through seasonal launches — storytelling on a grid, timed to the mountains
- The testing roadmap: landing pages, product-page content, checkout friction
- Email and retention programs with our marketing coordinator
- Fulfilment and customer-experience coordination with our warehouse partner during peaks
- A junior e-commerce coordinator (direct report)

You should have
- 3–5 years running or growing a direct-to-consumer online store, ideally in apparel or outdoor
- Fluency with modern e-commerce platforms, web analytics, and merchandising tools
- Sharp instincts for brand — we'd rather miss a promo than cheapen the label
- Spreadsheet-level comfort with margin math, cohort retention, and inventory turns

Compensation
$80,000–$100,000 (BC pay-transparency range), seasonal gear allowance, staff discount you will absolutely use, extended benefits, and a dog-friendly office fifteen minutes from the trailhead.

title: Product Manager, Platform
description:
Northstar Transit Tech builds real-time passenger information and fleet-management software for mid-sized transit agencies across North America. Forty-one agencies run their daily service on our platform.

The role
We're hiring a Product Manager for our platform group — the APIs, data pipelines, and admin tooling every customer-facing product depends on.

What you'll do
- Own the platform roadmap: prioritize ruthlessly across four internal teams and a public API consumed by agency developers
- Turn ambiguous agency needs (procurement language and all) into crisp problem statements
- Ship API and data-product improvements with clear versioning and migration stories
- Define metrics that capture platform health beyond uptime
- Spend real time with transit planners, dispatchers, and ops staff — our users work in control rooms, not conference rooms

You bring
- 3+ years of product management on technical or platform products
- Comfort reading API specs and asking engineers precise questions
- Experience in B2B or B2G software; patience for long procurement cycles
- Excellent written communication — PRDs, release notes, and executive one-pagers

Compensation
$115,000–$140,000 (Ontario posting range) plus bonus, RRSP matching, comprehensive benefits, hybrid (two days at our downtown office near Union), and a transit pass, obviously.

title: Graphic Designer
description:
Bluffside Creative is a Saskatoon design studio working with credit unions, universities, agriculture brands, and the arts community across the Prairies. We're a team of nine hiring a Graphic Designer who's equally at home in brand systems and campaign work.

What you'll do
- Design across identity, print, packaging, and digital campaigns — often for the same client in the same month
- Take brand systems from concept boards through final production art
- Prepare press-ready files and manage proofs with local and national printers
- Adapt campaign creative across formats: transit shelters, social, annual reports, event environments
- Present work to clients with our creative director and, increasingly, on your own

Who we're looking for
- 2–4 years of studio or in-house design experience with a portfolio that shows craft and ideas
- Expert Adobe Creative Suite; production knowledge that printers respect
- Typography that holds up at both billboard and body-copy scale
- A collaborative, low-ego approach to critique
- Illustration, motion, or photography skills are welcome bonuses

Details
Salary commensurate with experience and competitive for the Saskatoon market, health benefits, profit-share after one year, summer Fridays, and a Riversdale studio with more plants than people. Please apply with a portfolio link — applications without one won't be reviewed.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Foxglove Health Tech builds triage and capacity-planning tools for hospital networks and provincial health authorities. Our models help emergency departments see the surge coming before the waiting room does.

About the role
This is a fully remote position open to candidates anywhere in Canada. The team is distributed across four provinces and meets in person twice a year.

What you'll do
- Develop and validate forecasting models for patient volumes, admissions, and bed capacity
- Work with messy, real health-system data — missingness, drift, and all — under strict privacy controls
- Partner with clinical advisors to make model outputs interpretable and honestly uncertain
- Ship models to production with our ML engineers: monitoring, retraining, and rollback are part of the job
- Write validation reports rigorous enough for hospital governance committees

What we're looking for
- Graduate degree in statistics, CS, epidemiology, or equivalent applied experience
- 3+ years of applied data science with production Python (pandas, scikit-learn ecosystem, modern ML tooling)
- Strong statistical judgment — you know when a time-series model is lying to you
- Experience with health data and privacy frameworks (PHIPA/PIPEDA) is a significant asset

Compensation
$120,000–$150,000, extended benefits including mental-health coverage that isn't a token amount, home-office budget, and four weeks vacation.

title: HR Generalist
description:
Pinegate HR Solutions provides outsourced human-resources services to growing companies in manufacturing, logistics, and professional services across the Lower Mainland. We're hiring an HR Generalist to serve a cluster of three long-term client accounts from our Burnaby office.

What you'll do
- Act as the day-to-day HR presence for client workforces totalling about 280 employees
- Run full-cycle recruitment for frontline and office roles alongside client managers
- Coach supervisors through performance conversations, accommodations, and terminations done right
- Administer onboarding, benefits enrolment, and HRIS records with clean documentation
- Keep client policies current with B.C. employment standards and WorkSafeBC requirements
- Support investigations with thorough, impartial notes

What we're looking for
- 3+ years of progressive HR experience, ideally spanning blue- and white-collar environments
- Working knowledge of B.C. employment law; CPHR designation or progress toward it is an asset
- The tact to deliver hard messages and the spine to deliver them anyway
- Comfort switching contexts quickly — three clients means three cultures

Offer
$68,000–$84,000 (BC pay-transparency range), extended health and dental, CPHR dues covered, mileage for client-site days, and a supportive senior consultant team behind you on the thorny files.

title: Bilingual Customer Support Specialist
description:
Lighthouse Claims administers home and auto insurance claims for several Canadian insurers. Our Gatineau contact centre is the calm voice policyholders reach on one of the worst days of their year — and we staff it with people who take that seriously.

Le rôle / The role
We're hiring Bilingual Customer Support Specialists (French/English) for full-time weekday schedules between 8 AM and 8 PM. After training (fully on-site, four weeks), a hybrid schedule of three home days is available.

What you'll do
- Open new claims with empathy and precision, capturing details that adjusters depend on
- Answer status questions and explain next steps in plain language, in both official languages
- Coordinate with adjusters, contractors, and rental partners to keep files moving
- De-escalate frustrated callers without transferring your stress to the next one
- Document every interaction accurately in our claims platform

What we're looking for
- Fluent spoken and written French and English (tested during hiring)
- 1+ year in customer service — contact centre, retail, hospitality all count
- Steady typing while listening; our systems reward multitaskers
- Reliability — your team genuinely feels your absence

What we offer
Competitive salary reviewed annually, full benefits after three months, paid training, bilingual premium, free parking, and a management team promoted almost entirely from the phones.

title: Journeyperson Electrician
description:
Ridgeline Utilities maintains electrical infrastructure for industrial and institutional clients across the Avalon Peninsula — pumping stations, processing facilities, hospitals, and port operations. We're hiring a Journeyperson Electrician based out of our St. John's shop.

The work
- Install, maintain, and troubleshoot industrial electrical systems: motor controls, MCCs, VFDs, PLCs, and distribution up to 600V
- Perform preventive maintenance under our contract schedules and respond to corrective calls
- Read and mark up electrical drawings; leave installations better documented than you found them
- Participate in an on-call rotation (one week in five, premium-paid, callouts genuinely infrequent)
- Mentor apprentices and uphold our safety program without shortcuts — lockout is a ritual here, not a suggestion

Requirements
- Red Seal Construction or Industrial Electrician certification (Newfoundland and Labrador licence or eligibility)
- 3+ years post-journeyperson experience, industrial preferred
- Valid driver's licence; company service van provided for on-call weeks
- Comfort working at heights and in marine-adjacent environments

Compensation
$85,000–$102,000 including standard overtime patterns, on-call and callout premiums on top, full family benefits, defined-contribution pension with 5% matching, tool and boot allowances, and steady year-round work — no seasonal layoffs.

title: Technical Program Manager
description:
Snowfield Games operates a live multiplayer title with two million monthly players and a content cadence that never sleeps. Our Vancouver studio is hiring a Technical Program Manager to keep our live-operations machine running smoothly across four development teams.

What you'll do
- Own the release train: coordinate seasonal content drops, client patches, and server deployments across engineering, art, design, and QA
- Run risk tracking that surfaces problems while they're still cheap
- Facilitate cross-team dependencies — the economy team and the infrastructure team should never discover each other's plans in a post-mortem
- Tune our development process pragmatically; we care about flow, not ceremony compliance
- Communicate status honestly upward and outward, including the uncomfortable parts

What we're looking for
- 4+ years in technical program or production management on live software — games, SaaS, or platform teams
- Enough technical depth to follow architecture discussions and smell schedule risk in them
- Calm authority in incident coordination
- A track record of making teams faster by removing things, not adding them

Package
$120,000–$145,000 (BC pay-transparency range), studio bonus plan, extended health with family coverage, RRSP matching, four weeks vacation, and a no-crunch policy with receipts.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Meadowbrook Insurance is a Saskatchewan-based property and casualty insurer with 340 employees across the province. Our Regina head office is hiring a Payroll Administrator to join the people-services team.

Responsibilities
- Process semi-monthly payroll for salaried and hourly employees accurately and on schedule
- Administer new hires, terminations, leaves, and salary changes in the payroll and HRIS systems
- Reconcile payroll accounts, remittances, and year-end filings (T4s, taxable benefits, EHT-equivalents)
- Manage benefits and pension deductions, including adjustments during leaves
- Respond to employee questions with patience and airtight confidentiality
- Support internal and external audits with clean, organized records

Qualifications
- 2+ years of full-cycle Canadian payroll experience
- PCP designation (or active progress toward it — we cover the courses)
- Strong Excel and meticulous reconciliation habits
- Knowledge of Saskatchewan employment standards and multi-provincial payroll is an asset (we have small teams in two other provinces)
- The discretion this role demands; you'll know things before anyone else does

What we offer
Competitive salary reviewed annually, defined-benefit pension (increasingly rare, we know), full benefits, 35-hour work week, hybrid schedule after training, and free downtown parking.

title: Territory Sales Representative
description:
Copperhead Brewing is one of Alberta's fastest-growing independent craft breweries, pouring in 600 licensed accounts and 350 retail stores. We're hiring a Territory Sales Representative for Edmonton and the surrounding region.

What you'll do
- Own a territory of roughly 140 accounts: liquor stores, restaurants, bars, and event venues
- Grow distribution, secure taps and shelf placements, and defend them like they're your own
- Execute merchandising standards — coolers faced, pricing current, displays built
- Launch seasonal releases with account staff trainings and tastings (evening events roughly twice monthly)
- Track visits, orders, and opportunities in our CRM without being chased
- Work with our delivery team to keep service tight and out-of-stocks rare

Who you are
- 1–3 years in beverage, CPG, or hospitality sales — or bar/retail management ready to move to the supplier side
- A self-directed route planner who doesn't need an audience to work hard
- Clean Class 5 licence; you'll drive a branded company vehicle
- Genuine enthusiasm for craft beer and the people who sell it (ProServe required before start)

Compensation
Base salary plus uncapped monthly commission and quarterly bonuses — strong reps out-earn the posted market comfortably. Company vehicle, phone, benefits, and a generous beer allowance handled responsibly.

title: Solutions Architect (Pre-Sales)
description:
Switchback Software sells an integration platform used by enterprises to connect ERPs, warehouses, and storefronts without brittle point-to-point glue. Our sales engineering team is the technical spine of every deal, and we're hiring a Solutions Architect.

About the role
Fully remote within Canada, partnered with two enterprise account executives covering national accounts. Expect roughly 20% travel for discovery workshops and executive briefings.

What you'll do
- Lead technical discovery with customer architects and translate findings into winning solution designs
- Build and deliver demos and proofs-of-concept that map to the customer's actual systems, not a canned fantasy
- Answer security reviews and RFP technical sections with precision (and reusable assets you'll help build)
- Scope implementations honestly so delivery inherits promises they can keep
- Feed the product team structured field intelligence: what we lose on, and why

What we're looking for
- 5+ years in solutions architecture, sales engineering, or integration consulting
- Real depth in APIs, event-driven patterns, authentication, and at least one major cloud ecosystem
- The rare combination: technical credibility with architects AND clarity with executives
- Self-management worthy of a remote, travel-flexible role

Compensation
$140,000–$175,000 base plus variable tied to team quota (roughly 25% at target), equity, full benefits, home-office setup, and an annual team offsite somewhere with mountains.

title: Database Administrator
description:
Owl Creek Data provides managed database operations for mid-sized companies that need enterprise-grade reliability without an enterprise headcount. From our Edmonton operations centre we manage several hundred production databases for clients in healthcare, logistics, and public services.

The role
We're hiring a Database Administrator with deep PostgreSQL experience (we also run some SQL Server and MySQL estates — breadth welcome, PostgreSQL depth required).

What you'll do
- Own performance for client databases: query tuning, indexing strategy, vacuum and bloat management
- Design and TEST backup and recovery procedures — restores are rehearsed here, never improvised
- Plan and execute version upgrades and migrations with minimal downtime
- Configure replication and failover topologies appropriate to each client's tolerance
- Respond to escalations in a compensated on-call rotation (one week in six)
- Write post-incident and capacity reports clients can take to their boards

Requirements
- 4+ years of production DBA experience, with strong PostgreSQL internals knowledge
- Fluency in explain plans, lock analysis, and the difference between symptoms and causes
- Scripting for automation (Bash, Python, or similar)
- Clear client-facing communication under pressure

Offer
$100,000–$125,000, on-call premiums, full benefits, RRSP matching, training budget with dedicated study time, and a certified-boring on-call rotation — our monitoring catches most things first.

title: Business Intelligence Analyst
description:
Seabright Analytics helps ocean-economy companies — aquaculture, shipping, port services — turn operational data into decisions. We're a Halifax-headquartered team of 30, hiring a Business Intelligence Analyst.

About the role
Remote-first within Atlantic Canada: work from anywhere in the region, with monthly team days at our Halifax waterfront office.

What you'll do
- Build and maintain dashboards our clients open every morning: vessel utilization, feed conversion, berth scheduling, cost per unit
- Write the SQL behind them — clean, documented models in our warehouse, not spaghetti behind a chart
- Sit with client operations teams to understand what decision each number should drive
- Prototype analyses that graduate into product features when they prove their worth
- Maintain data-quality checks and chase anomalies to their source

What we're looking for
- 2–4 years in analytics, BI, or data-heavy operations roles
- Strong SQL (joins, window functions, CTEs) and experience with at least one modern BI platform
- Statistical common sense and the honesty to say 'the data can't answer that'
- Interest in physical industries; sea legs optional but appreciated on client visits

Compensation
$75,000–$92,000 depending on experience, health and dental, home-office allowance, four weeks vacation, and a company deeply unbothered by you leaving early to catch the tide.

title: Retail Operations Manager
description:
Kilnworks Home is a growing housewares and décor retailer with nine stores across Québec and an expanding online channel. We're hiring a Retail Operations Manager based at our Laval flagship and support office.

Le poste / The role
You'll own operational excellence across the store network: the systems, standards, and rhythms that let store teams focus on customers. Bilingual French/English required; our store teams work primarily in French.

Responsibilities
- Develop and roll out operating standards: opening/closing routines, cash handling, loss prevention, visual resets
- Own inventory integrity across stores and the warehouse — cycle counts, shrink analysis, transfer discipline
- Coordinate seasonal changeovers and new-store openings (two planned in the next 18 months)
- Manage vendor relationships for store supplies, maintenance, and security
- Coach store managers on scheduling, labour budgets, and operational KPIs
- Be the calm phone call when a store's day goes sideways

Profile
- 4+ years in multi-store retail operations or strong single-store management ready to scale
- Numbers fluency: labour models, shrink, sell-through
- Systems comfort — POS, inventory management, scheduling platforms
- Willingness to travel across Québec regularly (mileage covered)

Conditions
Competitive salary with annual bonus, employee discount, group insurance, and a leadership team that answers its own phones.

title: Civil Engineering Technologist
description:
Ferrostrand Rail Services designs and maintains short-line rail infrastructure for industrial clients across Québec and Eastern Ontario — spurs, sidings, crossings, and the drainage that keeps them standing. Our Sherbrooke office is hiring a Civil Engineering Technologist.

What you'll do
- Produce and revise drawings in AutoCAD and Civil 3D for track, grading, and drainage projects
- Conduct site inspections and condition assessments, including annual track audits with our engineers
- Process survey data and prepare quantity takeoffs and cost estimates
- Assist with construction supervision during summer work blocks: staking, testing coordination, daily reports
- Maintain project documentation to a standard our railway clients and regulators expect

Profile
- DEC in civil engineering technology or equivalent
- 2+ years in civil, transportation, or municipal projects (rail experience is a bonus we'll happily teach around)
- Proficient AutoCAD/Civil 3D; comfort with survey equipment an asset
- French working proficiency required; English an asset for Ontario clients
- Valid driver's licence and willingness for regular day-travel to sites (vehicle provided)

Conditions
$68,000–$85,000 depending on experience, field premiums, group insurance, RRSP contribution, professional-dues coverage, and Fridays that end at noon all summer.

title: Talent Acquisition Specialist
description:
Halcyon Senior Living operates eleven retirement and assisted-living residences across Alberta, employing more than 1,400 people who make our communities feel like home. Our Calgary support office is hiring a Talent Acquisition Specialist.

What you'll do
- Run full-cycle recruitment for high-volume frontline roles (health care aides, culinary, housekeeping) and targeted searches for nurses and site leadership
- Build sourcing pipelines that don't depend on job boards alone: schools, community programs, internationally educated professionals navigating licensure
- Screen with both speed and dignity — every applicant is a potential family member of a future resident
- Coach hiring managers on structured interviews and honest job previews
- Keep requisitions, offers, and onboarding handoffs organized in our HRIS/ATS
- Track metrics that matter: time-to-fill, 90-day retention, source quality

What we're looking for
- 2+ years of recruitment experience; healthcare, hospitality, or other high-volume environments preferred
- Empathy paired with throughput — this desk moves fast without feeling like it
- Familiarity with Alberta employment standards and healthcare screening requirements (or a quick study)

Offer
Competitive salary with annual review, benefits from day one, RRSP matching, on-site parking, and work that visibly matters every time you visit a residence you helped staff.

title: Executive Assistant
description:
Driftwood Coffee Roasters supplies cafés and grocers across Western Canada from our Richmond roastery, alongside three retail locations of our own. As we've grown past 90 employees, our two founders need real support. We're hiring an Executive Assistant.

What you'll do
- Own both founders' calendars, travel, and meeting preparation with an editor's judgment about what deserves their time
- Draft and polish communications: partner emails, board updates, internal announcements
- Prepare agendas and materials for leadership meetings; capture decisions and chase follow-ups to completion
- Coordinate company events, from quarterly all-hands at the roastery to the holiday party people actually attend
- Handle sensitive information — compensation, deals, personnel matters — with complete discretion
- Wrangle the small operational fires that don't belong to anyone else yet

Who thrives here
- 3+ years supporting executives or senior leaders in a fast-moving environment
- Writing skills strong enough that your drafts ship with light edits
- Calm, proactive, allergic to dropped balls
- Coffee enthusiasm optional; we'll convert you regardless

Details
$58,000–$72,000 (BC pay-transparency range), extended benefits, profit-share after one year, staff coffee benefit measured in kilograms, and an on-site role at the roastery with occasional flexibility.

title: Commercial HVAC Technician
description:
Ironvale Mechanical services commercial HVAC and refrigeration systems across the Edmonton region — office towers, grocery stores, light industrial, and institutional buildings. Our service division is growing and we're hiring a Commercial HVAC Technician.

The work
- Diagnose and repair rooftop units, boilers, chillers, make-up air units, and building controls
- Run scheduled preventive maintenance routes with a well-stocked, late-model service van
- Handle refrigeration calls on supermarket racks and walk-ins (an asset — we'll train the right foundation)
- Write clear service reports and quotes customers can actually understand
- Rotate through on-call one week in six with genuine premiums, not token ones

What we're looking for
- Journeyperson Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Mechanic ticket (or 3rd/4th year apprentice close to completion)
- Alberta B licence for gas work an asset
- 3+ years of commercial service experience preferred
- Clean Class 5 licence and a customer-facing manner buildings managers ask for by name

Compensation
$75,000–$95,000 depending on ticket and experience, with overtime and on-call premiums above that. Full benefits, RRSP matching, tool allowance, boot allowance, phone, and paid training days every year — we keep our techs current, not just busy.

title: Sales Development Representative
description:
Brightgrid Energy sells energy-monitoring and load-management software to commercial building owners who are tired of paying for electricity nobody used. Our Vancouver go-to-market team is hiring a Sales Development Representative.

What the job actually is
- Research and prioritize commercial property portfolios that fit our best-customer profile
- Run structured outbound: personalized email sequences, calls, and event follow-ups
- Qualify inbound interest from our content and webinar programs
- Book discovery meetings for account executives with context they can use, not just a calendar slot
- Keep the CRM accurate because your pipeline data steers real decisions
- Learn the energy domain properly — utility rates, demand charges, retrofit incentives — so your outreach sounds like it comes from someone worth meeting

Who does well here
- 0–2 years of experience; recent grads with hustle and curiosity are genuinely welcome
- Excellent written communication and a thick-enough skin for the phones
- Organization that survives 60 active conversations
- Interest in climate and buildings — you'll be talking about both all day

Compensation and path
$55,000–$65,000 base (BC pay-transparency range) plus commission on qualified meetings and closed-won influence; realistic first-year earnings $70,000–$85,000. Clear 18-month promotion path to account executive, benefits, transit subsidy, and hybrid schedule.

title: Marketing Coordinator
description:
Quillfeather Publishing is an independent Atlantic Canadian publisher of fiction, poetry, and regional non-fiction, with a catalogue of 300 titles and a fiercely loyal readership. Our Fredericton office is hiring a Marketing Coordinator.

What you'll do
- Plan and publish social content across our channels: new releases, author spotlights, backlist gems
- Build our monthly reader newsletter and seasonal catalogue emails, then study what people actually clicked
- Coordinate book launches, festival appearances, and author tours across the Maritimes (some travel, mostly delightful)
- Draft press releases and pitch regional media, bookstagrammers, and podcast hosts
- Manage review-copy mailings and our awards-submission calendar
- Update our website and keep retailer metadata accurate so books are findable everywhere they're sold

Who we're looking for
- 1–3 years in marketing, communications, publicity, or bookselling
- Writing that's clean, warm, and quick — you'll draft a dozen different things in a week
- Comfort with email platforms, social scheduling tools, and light graphics work
- Genuine love of books and the patience for an industry that runs on long timelines and small margins

Details
Salary competitive for the New Brunswick market and commensurate with experience, health benefits, generous book allowance, four weeks of holidays including the quiet week between Christmas and New Year, and an office above a bookshop, which is exactly as good as it sounds.

title: IT Support Specialist
description:
Bayline Ferries operates passenger and vehicle ferry services on Atlantic routes, with our operations and administrative headquarters in Moncton. Our small IT team keeps reservations, terminals, and vessels connected — and we're adding an IT Support Specialist.

What you'll do
- Provide first- and second-line support for about 220 staff across head office, terminals, and vessels
- Image, deploy, and manage Windows laptops and terminal workstations; administer accounts and permissions in our directory
- Support the reservation and point-of-sale systems our terminals depend on during sailings — outages here are measured in lineups
- Maintain network basics at remote sites: switches, access points, VPN connectivity (with a managed-services partner for the heavy lifting)
- Document fixes properly so the next occurrence takes ten minutes
- Occasional travel to terminal sites, ferry rides included

What we're looking for
- 2+ years in IT support or help-desk roles
- Solid Windows administration; scripting basics an asset
- Networking fundamentals you can troubleshoot with, not just define
- Patience for users mid-crisis at a busy terminal counter, and the judgment to escalate early when it's real

What we offer
Competitive salary based on experience, defined-contribution pension, full benefits, ferry travel privileges for your household, and a role where 'the systems stayed up all summer' is a sentence people thank you for.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Cloudberry Systems builds document-intelligence software used by insurers and government agencies to process claims, permits, and correspondence in both official languages. Our Québec City lab is hiring a Machine Learning Engineer.

What you'll do
- Train, evaluate, and ship models for document classification, extraction, and bilingual NLP tasks
- Build the MLOps backbone with our platform team: reproducible training pipelines, model registries, monitored deployments, honest rollbacks
- Design evaluation suites that reflect messy production documents, not leaderboard conditions — including French/English parity as a first-class metric
- Optimize inference for cost and latency on realistic hardware budgets
- Work with product and compliance colleagues on explainability requirements for public-sector clients

Profile
- 3+ years building and deploying ML systems in production
- Strong PyTorch and modern NLP experience, including fine-tuning transformer models
- Software engineering discipline: your notebooks graduate into tested code
- French or English working proficiency required; comfort in both is a real asset given our bilingual data

Compensation
$125,000–$155,000 depending on experience, annual bonus, four weeks vacation, full group insurance, conference budget, and a lab in Saint-Roch with the best coffee within three postal codes.
